units.source_text: 紫夫人死而复生之后，源氏更加恐惧不安，便重新举办法事，比以前隆重得多。

en.t: After Lady Murasaki came back from the brink of death, Genji grew even more fearful and uneasy, and he held another Buddhist service, far grander than before.

units.source_text: 当年六条妃子在世，其生魂尚且可怕得很，何况现已隔世，变成怪异的鬼魂。

en.t: In earlier years, while Lady Rokujo was still alive, her living spirit had already been terrifying; how much more so now that she had passed beyond this world and become a strange ghost.

units.source_text: 源氏仔细想想，实在气愤得很，连照顾秋好皇后的心，一时也懈怠了。

en.t: The more carefully Genji thought about it, the more deeply angered he became, and for a time even his concern for Empress Akikonomu slackened.

units.source_text: 推而广之，他觉得女人都是万般罪恶的根源。

en.t: Extending that thought further, he came to feel that women were the root of every kind of evil.

units.source_text: 更进一步，又觉得世间一切都可厌了。

en.t: Going still further, he began to feel that everything in the world was hateful.

units.source_text: 那天他和紫夫人两人畅谈心事之时，曾经约略提及六条妃子，并无别人听见，而那鬼魂竟会说得出来。

en.t: On that day, when he and Lady Murasaki had spoken openly together of their innermost feelings, they had only briefly mentioned Lady Rokujo, with no one else there to hear it, yet that ghost had somehow been able to speak of it.

units.source_text: 如此看来，这鬼魂确是六条妃子，这便使他更加烦恼了。

en.t: Seen in that light, the ghost was indeed Lady Rokujo, and this troubled him even more.

units.source_text: 紫夫人近来一心要祝发为尼，源氏推想佛力可以使她恢复健康，便把她顶上的头发略微剪下少许，教她受了五戒。

en.t: Lady Murasaki had lately been intent on shaving her head and becoming a nun, and Genji, thinking that the power of the Buddha might restore her health, cut a small amount of hair from the crown of her head and had her receive the five precepts.

units.source_text: 授戒法师将受戒无量功德在佛前宣读，文词备极庄严。

en.t: The monk who conferred the precepts read aloud before the Buddha of the immeasurable merit of receiving them, in words of the utmost solemnity.

units.source_text: 源氏不顾体统，只管傍在紫夫人身边，揩着眼泪，和她一起念佛。

en.t: Genji paid no heed to appearances, but stayed close beside Lady Murasaki, wiping away his tears as he recited the Buddha's name together with her.

units.source_text: 观此情状，可知世间无论何等高贵贤明的人，遇到此种患难之事，也是不得安稳的。

en.t: Seeing such a scene, one understands that no matter how noble or wise a person may be, when faced with this kind of suffering, they cannot remain at peace.

units.source_text: 无论何事，只要是能却病延年的，无不做到。

en.t: Whatever might ward off illness and prolong life, he left nothing undone.

units.source_text: 源氏昼夜忧愁悲叹，弄得神思恍惚，面庞也稍稍瘦削了。

en.t: Day and night Genji grieved and lamented, until his mind grew dazed and his face became a little thinner.
